title: Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B) Deep Dive Analysis
summary: Financial-sector value depends on solvency, fiscal support and rates.
coverage_note: All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

claims.claim: Full job recovery will be slow
claims.reason: Payroll employment did not return to its February 2020 level until July 2022 in the contemporary release. That supports the distinction between a reopening bounce and full recovery. Continued claims are beneficiaries, however, not an exact count of all lost jobs.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

evidence.title: July 2022 Employment Situation release
evidence.finding: The release reported payroll employment and unemployment rate had returned to February 2020 levels in July 2022. This is a publication-vintage recovery date, not a claim about subsequently revised payroll history.

claims.claim: Benefit expiry creates a fiscal dilemma
claims.conditions: Jobs do not rebound almost fully
claims.reason: Substantial additional fiscal support ultimately arrived, including ARP. This supports the continued-support branch, but does not verify the predicted late-summer timing or a reacceleration of QE specifically caused by benefit expiry.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

evidence.title: About the American Rescue Plan
evidence.finding: ARP passed Congress March 10, 2021 and was signed March 11. Treasury managed over $1 trillion in its programs and tax credits, confirming further large fiscal support after 2020.

evidence.title: Federal Reserve total assets
evidence.finding: Weekly total assets rose from $4.183 trillion on February 12, 2020 to $4.242 trillion March 4 and $6.368 trillion April 15. A brief late-February decline preceded the surge.

claims.claim: Generous benefits weaken work incentives
claims.reason: Replacement rates can alter incentives, but pandemic health risk, child care and unavailable jobs confound observed employment. A causal estimate comparing otherwise similar eligible workers is needed.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

claims.claim: Retail enthusiasm is unusually speculative
claims.reason: Brokerage activity, option buys and holdings counts measure different things. New-account anecdotes and a few bankrupt stocks do not establish aggregate investor performance or the source of counterparties.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Business performance and shareholder return are distinct.
claims.next_check: Verify broker DARTs, OCC customer opening transactions and archived Robintrack counts.

claims.claim: Changed fundamentals justify exiting losses
claims.reason: Carnival subsequently recorded severe losses, dilution and restrictions. This supports revising the operating premise; the original recommendation remains a separate score, and author-reported execution is not independently audited.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

evidence.title: Fiscal 2020 Form 10-K
evidence.finding: FY 2020 net loss was $10.236 billion, versus $2.990 billion profit in 2019. Weighted average shares rose from 690 million to 775 million. Dividend stopped after first quarter; financing restricted future payments.

claims.claim: Ambev has stronger income-portfolio resilience
claims.reason: Ambev maintained net cash and profitability; Cheesecake halted its dividend and needed preferred financing. This supports financial resilience, without establishing replacement-trade total return.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Business performance and shareholder return are distinct.

evidence.title: Financial highlights 2015-2025
evidence.finding: 2020 EPS R$0.72 versus 0.75 in 2019, 2021 R$0.81, 2025 R$0.99.2020 net cash R$14.0 b; 2025 R$16.9 b. 2020 EBITDA margin 37%,2022 29.8%,2025 33.4%, versus 40.2% in 2019. Per-share figures are issuer-adjusted for corporate actions.

evidence.title: Preliminary first-quarter fiscal 2020 results
evidence.finding: Q1 comparable sales fell 12.9%. Company suspended dividends, buybacks and new-unit development; obtained $200 million convertible preferred financing and covenant relief.

claims.claim: Banks offer better risk than airlines

evidence.title: How money is created
evidence.finding: Reserves are electronic central-bank settlement money. Capital is a separate resource that absorbs loan-default losses; both liquidity and capital constraints apply to banks.

claims.claim: QE recapitalizes banks through reserves
claims.reason: A market-value exchange of securities for reserves improves liquidity but does not automatically increase equity capital. If the seller is a nonbank, the bank gains a reserve asset and matching deposit liability. Loss absorption requires capital, profits, guarantees or direct recapitalization, not merely a larger reserve balance.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

claims.claim: Succession can cause a stock decline
claims.reason: CEO succession was announced in May 2025; BRK-B fell 5.12% from May 2 to May 5. This matches the event-risk direction, although simultaneous results and Buffett remaining chairman prevent clean causal attribution.

evidence.finding: Buffett announced succession recommendation May 3, 2025; board unanimously approved Greg Abel as CEO effective January 1, 2026, with Buffett then remaining chairman.

evidence.finding: Archived BRK-B closes: May 2, 2025 $539.79999; May 5 $512.15002, a 5.12% decline across the succession-announcement weekend. Earnings news was also contemporaneous, so the return is not a causal isolation.

framework_lessons: Liquidity buffers and equity capital solve different problems.
assessment: The delayed job recovery, bank earnings decline and fiscal-reflation direction were supported. The expected Treasury yield-control regime failed. Reserve creation is repeatedly confused with bank recapitalization, a material mechanistic error. Berkshire succession risk matched an observed decline, while the post-succession restructuring thesis remains early.

Public market series are available, but not every investment claim has a defined horizon or reconciled corporate-action-adjusted return. Unverified outcomes remain unscored; macro data use latest available vintages.
